loggia_thermal_consequence.finding: !! THE ЛОДЖИЯ IS THERMALLY DECOUPLED FROM THE FLAT, AND THAT CUTS AGAINST THE OWNER'S OWN GOAL.
reasoning: The wall between the flat and the лоджия - M1, plus M7 and the insulated face of R8 - is full warm perimeter: 300 mm block with 70 mm of mineral wool.
So essentially NO heat leaks from the heated flat into the лоджия. One might otherwise have assumed some did.
M2 separates this лоджия from the neighbour's, and both are unheated - cold-to-cold, no help from that side either.
The лоджия's own enclosure is thin and uninsulated by design: M2 'thinner', M6b ~200 mm provisional.
The floor and ceiling are slabs shared with the loggias above and below, which are also unheated.
loggia_thermal_consequence.consequence: !! THE STANDING TARGET - keep the лоджия frost-free through an ordinary Belarusian winter with NO heating, on passive measures alone - therefore rests on exactly two things: SOLAR GAIN, and the лоджия's OWN enclosure. Nothing is contributed by the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_good_news: Solar gain is the best it could be: the лоджия's main angled glazing faces DUE SOUTH (confirmed orientation), making it the most solar-exposed element in the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_work: So the glazing upgrade the owner is already planning is doing nearly all of the work, and the thin uninsulated enclosure walls (M2, M6b) are the weak points. Whether the target is achievable at all is an open question the vault has already flagged as a content gap - see 00_Master/Family_Requirements.md section 10 - and this is the constraint set that question has to be answered against.
loggia_thermal_consequence.note_on_scope: The owner has decided NOT to join the лоджия to the flat and to keep its doors and windows. That decision is unaffected; what changes is where the heat has to come from.

three_ways_they_behave_unlike_walls: 1. IMMOVABLE - common property serving the whole riser. No layout variant may touch them.

CORRECTED_2026_09_04.why: The passway is the gap between V2's end and R5. V2 is 455 mm SHORTER on the 4th floor than on the detailed plan I measured from, so the gap is that much wider.

Worth checking each product's PACKED size before ordering, not after - and it connects to the vault's specify-large-and-cut finding, whose third motive is exactly access.
It also explains the прихожая's shape and its 9.79 m²: the hall is bounded on that side by a shaft plus a column rather than by a wall.

kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.finding: !!! THERE IS NO WALL between the кухня (5.24) and the living room (19.49). Verified on the detailed plan at 5x: the only things on that line are a DASHED zone boundary and a DASH-DOT grid axis. No hatching, no thickness, no jambs.

kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.what_it_invalidates: !! Two of the four arguments recorded earlier for v1's kitchen move are WITHDRAWN. The DAYLIGHT argument ("merging it into the living room is the only way that zone gets daylight") fails because they are already one space, so the zone already borrows the living room's window - badly, being at the far end from the glazing, but "no daylight" was wrong. kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.how_both_failed_the_same_way: !! I checked whether the KITCHEN had an external wall and never checked whether it was an ENCLOSED ROOM. A zone label on a plan is not a room, and I treated it as one for four rounds.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.what_survives: The owner's SEPARABILITY thesis, which was always the primary reason and depends on none of this; and the acoustics point about the middle room, which concerns a different room. But the review's claim of "three independent arguments" is now one.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.the_rule: !!! A LABEL ON A PLAN IS NOT A ROOM. The кухня had an area, a name, a printed dimension chain and fixtures drawn in it - everything a room has except walls. Before treating any labelled space as enclosed, CHECK ITS BOUNDARY FOR HATCHING.

junction_convention_2026_09_04.rule: !! Every wall length is the CLEAR INTERNAL run, face to face between its neighbours. No wall’s length includes any part of a wall it touches, and no two wall solids may overlap.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.owner_wording: "R1a and R1b are crossing at the corner, that shouldn’t be so - the walls cannot overlap. When we calculate the length of a wall section we should take a look at the thickness of the one it is adjacent to, because we shouldn’t double count the thickness of the walls."
junction_convention_2026_09_04.the_other_half_of_it: Nothing is double-counted, which was his point - but nothing may be silently UNDER-counted either. Corner and T-junction volumes belong to no wall under this convention, so they are carried as a separate junction allowance rather than quietly lost from the quantities.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.why_it_is_also_the_practical_choice: It matches how the flat will actually be measured in three months: a tape held inside a room reads the clear run.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.enforced_by: tools/layout/check_wall_crossings.py, over data/canonical/wall_runs.csv. Run it after any change to the geometry.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.what_the_sweep_found: !! The owner spotted R1a x R1b (147 mm overlap). Sweeping all 25 runs found a SECOND instance he had not spotted: G2 x G4C (166 mm), where G4C was drawn running through the top wall. Both fixed. That is precisely why this became a script rather than a habit - one crossing was visible and the other was not, and the difference between them was luck.
junction_convention_2026_09_04.SUPERSEDED: !! The "separate junction allowance" half of this entry was WRONG and is replaced by corner_ownership_2026_09_04. Clear-internal-everywhere cannot double-count a corner, but it leaves every L-corner unfilled - and the owner is right that a void is as wrong as an overlap. The clear-run rule itself stands; what changes is that corners are OWNED, not allowanced.

corner_ownership_2026_09_04.owner_wording: "One bad thing is overlapping. Another bad thing is creating a void. A correct junction is, for example, MA and R8, R8 and MB - a perfect corner when you take the thickness into account. If we connect R1a and R1b we get a void at the very corner. You should extend either R1b or R1a by the thickness, 250 mm. And the same 250 to either G3 or R2."
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.rule: !! Every wall carries TWO lengths. clear_mm is what the plan prints and what a tape held inside the room reads. solid_mm is clear_mm plus the thickness of every corner THAT wall owns. At each L-corner exactly one wall runs through to the other’s far face and the other stops on its near face, so the corner volume is counted once - never twice, never zero times.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.ownership_is_deterministic: 1: the thicker wall owns the corner (the envelope beats a partition). 2: on a tie, the longer run (the continuous line beats a stub). 3: on a tie, alphabetically first, only so the output is stable.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.why_that_rule_is_trusted: Rule 1 independently reproduces the two junctions the owner named as ALREADY CORRECT - MA over R8 and MB over R8 - without being told which walls are external. That is the test that it is the right rule rather than a convenient one.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.the_ten_corners: MB +250 +250 = +500 (R8 and R9, at both its ends) · R1a +250 · G3 +250 · MA +250 · G4a +120 · R1b +120 · G4d +75 · R4 +75 · R5 +75. Every other wall: solid_mm = clear_mm. G3’s +250 applies to the R3+G3 pair, whose solid run is therefore 5830 + 250 = 6080 - exactly what the owner’s own top-edge chain does when it appends R2’s thickness after the 3315.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.MY_FIRST_ATTEMPT_WAS_THE_WRONG_INSTRUMEN: !! I first wrote a resolver that snapped the drawn pixel runs until every corner closed. It moved R2 by 27 mm, G8 by 77 and G4d by 58 - figures that come from printed dimensions and the owner’s own chains - in order to satisfy a raster registration only good to ~50 mm. Deleted. The drawing LOCATES walls; the printed dimensions DEFINE them. The corner decision belongs in the lengths, not in the picture. This is the same lesson as junction_correction_2026_09_04 (blob edges locate, printed dimensions fix) arriving in a new disguise, and I did not recognise it until the diff showed his numbers moving.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.what_the_sweep_found_beyond_what_he_name: He named R1a×R1b and G3×R2. Checking all 25 runs found 8 voids and 3 bad T-junctions, including G4C drawn CROSSING G4d and G4d ending 203 mm short of G4a’s face. All fixed.

corner_ownership_2026_09_04.RULE_CORRECTED_the_frame_owns_the_corner: !! Rule 1 was "the thicker wall owns the corner". WRONG, and the owner’s own arithmetic falsified it within the hour. The rule is THE CONCRETE FRAME OWNS THE CORNER: the developer’s description, already in building_spec.json, reads "монолитный железобетонный каркас с наружными стенами (не несущие) из блоков" - the frame is cast first and the blocks are non-load-bearing infill built against it. So a 250 concrete column owns its corner even where a 300+70 block wall meets it. Order is now: frame, then thicker, then longer, then alphabetical.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.why_the_correction_is_certain: It reproduces every figure the owner had computed independently, where "thicker wins" reproduced none: R2 = 1675 clear + 250 = 1925 (his arithmetic, verbatim); R8 = 1490 + 300 = 1790 and R9 the same (the figure he "remembered"). His numbers chose the rule.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.and_it_settles_the_1925_argument: !! R2 = 1925 is the exact number the owner corrected me on two rounds earlier. Both of us were right: 1675 is the CLEAR run and 1925 is the SOLID. They are different quantities and the model now carries both, so neither has to win. My error was never the 1925 - it was calling it the internal dimension.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.the_eight_corners: R1a +250 · R1b +120 · R2 +250 · R4 +75 · R5 +75 · R8 +300 +300 · R9 +300. Every owner is a concrete frame member, which is the rule showing its work. Every other wall: solid_mm = clear_mm.
corner_ownership_2026_09_04.v19_still_DREW_the_void: ⚠ The owner had to raise the same objection twice. v19 put the ownership in the ledger and in the labels but left the DRAWING showing clear runs - so R1a still stopped at R1b’s face while MC ran through R7, two corners drawn two ways in one drawing. corner_ownership_2026_09_04.a_thin_partition_is_a_BUTT_not_a_corner: !! Rule 0, added 2026-09-04. A partition of 120 mm or less meeting a concrete frame member forms a BUTT, never a corner: it lands on the column’s face and the column does not wrap around it, so neither length changes. The owner’s wording, about R4 and R5: "the length is clear, it is 1050, and that’s it - there is no hidden section, so no solid part." Encoding it as a rule rather than an exception drops R4, R5 AND R1b - leaving exactly the owners he named (R2, R8, R9) plus R1a, which he had asked to extend two rounds earlier. R1b he did not mention, but it is the same case as R4. Five corners now, down from ten.

collinear_successors_2026_09_04.this_is_where_the_printed_175_comes_from: 250 - 75 = 175 is the column PROJECTING past the partition that continues its own line. Both were phantom corners that would have added material twice.
